observations.observation: The earliest located secondary report on the Google/EMIB-T link is Tom’s Hardware on July 15, citing SemiAnalysis for a plan to use EMIB-T on a next-generation TPU called Humufish. This is reported intent, not a disclosed production commitment.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The article attributes the report to SemiAnalysis and does not establish an actual selection date, binding order, qualification completion, or company confirmation.

observations.observation: Counterpoint’s April 29 public research described EMIB-T for TPU v8e/Humufish as proposed and still in design-in/qualification; it said mass production was not targeted until late 2027. The model specificity is useful, but the September 30 wording “next-generation TPU” does not identify whether it is the same product.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The April statement is a prior research assessment, not an official Google/Intel status report; the later statement lacks generation-level detail, so a change in status for the same product cannot be established.

observations.observation: TrendForce’s September 18 pre-cutoff outlook expected Google to adopt EMIB-T in 2027 and noted AWS testing, while forecasting CoWoS-L to remain the mainstream solution through 2028 because of maturity and yield.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is an industry forecast and technical assessment; it does not confirm a completed Google adoption or quantify a package order.

observations.observation: Counterpoint’s September 29 Q2 market release reports the Foundry 2.0 and TSMC figures and packaging-capacity outlook. Its current indexed page includes an Intel/Google adoption statement, but the historical presence of that passage by cutoff could not be verified.
observations.event_time: Q2 2026 reporting period for the cited market figures
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: Do not use the current-page adoption sentence as pre-cutoff primary evidence without a dated original snapshot; contemporaneous EDaily separately reports the analyst statement on September 30.

observations.observation: EDaily reported at 19:07:59 KST (10:07:59Z) on September 30 that Counterpoint analyst William Li said EMIB-T had been adopted for Google’s next-generation TPU. It also reported his caveat on Intel’s relative process scale, yields and packaging execution.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The report is an analyst-attributed statement, not direct disclosure from Google or Intel; it provides no TPU model, qualification, binding order, volume or production timing. The English page is machine-translated.

observations.observation: Benzinga published the supplied story at 11:15:34Z, repeating the adoption statement attributed to Counterpoint, 1 minute 48 seconds before the evidence cutoff.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: This is later than the located EDaily report and does not add direct company confirmation, commercial terms, order quantity or production status.

gaps: No direct pre-cutoff Google or Intel disclosure confirming the reported adoption, naming the TPU generation/model, stating qualification completion, or documenting a binding order, reserved capacity, paid production packages, volume or shipment schedule was located in this bounded search.
The actual date and stage of any customer decision are unknown; the reports provide publication times, not the event time.
The Counterpoint September 29 page’s current indexed EMIB-T sentence lacks a verified pre-cutoff snapshot or revision history, so its presence in the original dated release cannot be established.
The phrase “next-generation TPU” in the September 30 reports is not model-specific; it cannot be confidently reconciled with Counterpoint’s earlier TPU v8e/Humufish status description.

The bounded search identifies the earliest located report and earliest time-stamped coverage, but cannot establish absolute first circulation or recover the original SemiAnalysis publication timestamp.
research_notes: Cutoff: 2026-09-30T11:17:22.645750Z. The earliest traceable public report located on Google using EMIB-T is Tom’s Hardware’s July 15 article, which attributes the report to SemiAnalysis; it describes a plan, not a confirmed production order. Counterpoint’s April report characterized EMIB-T for TPU v8e/Humufish as proposed and in design-in/qualification, with mass production not targeted until late 2027. TrendForce on September 18 likewise said adoption was expected in 2027 and identified CoWoS-L’s maturity and yield as continuing advantages. For the later “adopted” wording attributed to Counterpoint analyst William Li, the earliest time-stamped coverage found in this search was EDaily at 19:07:59 KST (10:07:59Z), before the Benzinga item at 11:15:34Z. The Benzinga item was published 1 minute 48 seconds before cutoff. Neither contemporaneous report supplies the TPU model, actual selection date, qualification status, binding order, production quantity, or customer/company confirmation. Counterpoint’s live September 29 page currently returns an EMIB-T adoption sentence, but no pre-cutoff snapshot or revision history was found to establish when that sentence appeared; it is not treated here as verified pre-cutoff primary evidence. No post-cutoff material or market reaction is used.
